newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SWISSAIR WRITEOFF COULD MEAN PULLOUT FROM SABENA.
newsitem.headline: SWISSAIR WRITEOFF COULD MEAN PULLOUT FROM SABENA.

text.p: Swissair is threatening the possibility of pulling out of Sabena by considering a writeoff of its investment in the Belgin airline, Sabena chief executive Paul Reutlinger said on Thursday.

"The threat is to write off the investment but what it means is to have the liberty to take any decision afterwards. (This includes) Swissair walking away," Reutlinger told Reuters after a news conference.
Swissair has a 49.5 percent stake in semi-state owned Sabena. Reutlinger said earlier Swissair might write off its investment if Sabena suffered further industrial dispute.
This write off could be made in financial year 1996 already.
A draft deal on a 4.7 billion Belgian franc recovery plan for the Belgian airline has been reached with the four Belgian trade unions involved.
However members of the pilots' association within the trade unions had pulled out of the negotiations two days ago and had begun strike action on Thursday.
Reutlinger said he had told striking pilots that Swissair was threatening to pull out of Sabena, and he would now resume negotiations with them.
